items.description: A collection of urban planning related data specifications and standards for use as part of programs & projects.

children.title: BLDS
children.description: The BLDS data standard is a collaborative effort by civic technology companies, governments and other interested parties to create a shared data specification for building and construction permit data.

children.title: DTDL
children.description: The Digital Twins Definition Language is the language by which developers can define the language of the entities they expect to use in their topologies.

children.title: SharedStreets
children.description: Referencing System is a global, non-proprietary linear referencing system for describing streets maintained by SharedStreets. Additional Information: GitHub

children.title: MDS
children.description: The Mobility Data Specification is a data standard to enable communication between mobility companies and local governments.

children.title: CDS
children.description: The Curb Data Specification provides data specifications for curb regulations alongside a connected event and metrics API intended to help cities manage their curb zone programs and surrounding areas, and measure the utilization and impact.

children.title: OpenSidewalks
children.description: A data specification for routable pedestrian networks and describing and sharing pedestrian network and pedestrian network-adjacent data.

children.title: shared-row
children.description: A data specification for representing street right of ways.

children.title: GBFS
children.description: The General Bikeshare Feed Specification is a standardized data feed for shared mobility system availability.

children.title: GTFS-flex
children.description: A data format that models flexible public transportation services (microtransit/paratransit) as an extension to GTFS.

children.title: GMNS
children.description: The General Modeling Network Specification defines a common human and machine readable format for sharing routable road network files.

children.title: MTLFS
children.description: The Managed and Tolled Lanes Feed Specification is intended to be used by the managed lanes and toll industry for the standardization and sharing of dynamic toll rates, and any managed lane purpose including but not limited to, ramp metering, bus only lanes, express lanes, especially if the resources are being priced dynamically.

items.title: Planning Data Specifications

items.description: This is a curated list of Python, R, or other open-source libraries or programming tools can be useful for urban planning applications.

children.title: UrbanSim
children.description: A platform for building statistical models of cities and regions. These models help forecast long-range patterns in real estate development, demographics, and related outcomes, under various policy scenarios. Information: License: BSD License: Provider: UrbanSim Inc. (UDST).

children.title: rasterio
children.description: Geographic information systems use GeoTIFF and other formats to organize and store gridded raster datasets such as satellite imagery and terrain models.

children.title: Geemap
children.description: A Python package for interactive mapping with Google Earth Engine, ipyleaflet, and ipywidgets.

children.title: StreetTraffic
children.description: A Python package that crawls the traffic flow data of your favorite routes, cities by using the API provided by HERE.

children.title: Pybikes
children.description: Provides a set of tools to scrape bike sharing data from different websites and APIs, thus providing a coherent and generalized set of classes and methods to access this sort of information.

children.title: Gleam
children.description: A plotting library inspired by R-Shiny to create interactive plots.

children.title: Geosnap
children.description: Geospatial & temporal neighborhood analysis using US Census Data.

children.title: Peartree
children.description: Helps explore GTFS data and their network characteristics.

children.title: HerePy
children.description: A library that provides a Python interface to HERE APIs.

children.title: OSMnx
children.description: Python for street networks. Retrieve, model, analyze, and visualize street networks and other spatial data from OpenStreetMap.

children.title: Prettymaps
children.description: A small set of Python functions to draw pretty maps from OpenStreetMap data.

children.title: Urbansprawl
children.description: The urbansprawl project provides an open source framework for assessing urban sprawl using open data. It uses OpenStreetMap (OSM) data to calculate its sprawling indices, divided in Accessibility, Land use mix, and Dispersion.

children.title: Leafmap
children.description: A free and open-source Python package that enables users to analyze and visualize geospatial data with minimal coding in a Jupyter environment. Leafmap's interactive GUI allows no code layer management and analysis including a powerful analytical backend (i.e., WhiteboxTools). Additional Information: leafmap.org, JOSS Article, Medium Article.

children.title: Neatnet
children.description: An open source library for simplifying the structure of street networks.

children.title: Madina
children.description: This is a package of classes and functions to streamline the representation and analysis of urban networks. This library includes a Python implementation of the Urban Network Analysis Tools.

children.title: Rgee
children.description: Is an R binding package for calling Google Earth Engine API from within R. Various functions are implemented to simplify the connection with the R spatial ecosystem.

children.title: r5r
children.description: Is an R package for rapid realistic routing on multimodal transport networks (walk, bike, public transport and car) leveraging the Conveyal R5 routing engine.

children.title: leafgl
children.description: R package for fast web-gl rendering for leaflet maps.

children.title: global-indicators
children.description: Case study projected dedicated to developing global healthy and sustainable city-indicators collaboration.

children.title: civic-tech-patterns
children.description: Common patterns and anti-patterns for civic tech and civic applications. Additional Information: Provided by Code for America.
